newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chemical groups eye modest production rise.
newsitem.headline: German chemical groups eye modest production rise.

text.p: The German chemical industry is eyeing a slight pickup in production in the coming months as higher foreign demand may help offset stagnant domestic conditions, leaving behind a soft beginning to the year.
"For the remainder of the year we largely expect a slightly more positive development as compared with year-ago levels," the German chemical industry association VCI said in a report.
Exports, which have been critical to several large companies' nine month results, are expected to rise further in coming months, the group forecast.
Meanwhile sluggish domestic economic conditions show few signs of abating, leaving the association to write "in the domestic market we only hope for a stabilistation of business."
Soft economic conditions have plagued the German chemical industry for nearly a year with January-to-August production levels falling 2.7 percent from year-ago levels.
In the first eight months of this year, German chemical groups sold 118.2 billion marks worth of goods, which was four percent less than in the same time last year.
"Weak domestic demand and soft producer prices clearly dented results," the group said.
The association's report closely mirrors German chemical giants Bayer AG and Hoechst AG's nine-month results, showing lower international prices and weak domestic demand.
But like Hoechst and Bayer, both modestly optimistic for the next several months, the association said "in the third quarter there were first signs that production levels will stabilise."

Prices in the German chemical industry during the first eight months of the year were 3.6 percent below year ago levels, indicating that companies were unable to push through price increases due to softer economic conditions.
As German companies seek to be closer to expanding international markets, foreign investment jumped by 10.3 percent in 1995, the association said.
Individual companies have also said the trend of growing investments abroad will continue, with many earmarking billions of marks for investment in Asia, particularly China.

The association reported that employment in the sector in the first eight months of the year was 3.2 percent lower than it was a year ago showing industry job cuts were continuing but at a slower pace than in past years.

The recession in the early 1990s hit the German chemical industry especially hard triggering massive job cuts as the companies scrambled to modernise and rationalise to keep pace with growing international competitors.
Among individual products, pharmaceutical exports, making up over 15 percent of the industry's total exports, jumped 9.3 percent in the first eight months of the year.
Meanwhile organic chemical exports dropped 6.2 percent and plastics dropped 5.8 percent.
